messages:
maria_supp: @acme_prod — quick heads up, we just got a support ticket saying replies became noticeably shorter and more abrupt after yesterday's model rollout. they included a couple of examples.
acme_prod: thanks, here's one that nails it down:
```
Prompt: "Summarize the project's deployment steps for non-technical PMs."
Before (v4.3.1): "Start by creating an infra plan that lists environments, owners, and rollback criteria. Then provision resources, run smoke tests, and schedule the cutover. Include post-deploy monitoring and a rollback playbook." (~85 tokens)
After (v4.4.0): "Create infra plan. Deploy. Monitor." (~18 tokens)
```
sam_eng: can you paste the raw responses or request ids? also which org and route? we need to triage ASAP.
maria_supp: request ids: req_9342, req_9343. org: acme_prod. Route: /generate-support-summary. Customer says change started right after 2026-03-08 02:00 UTC rollout.
julie_ml: interesting. Possibilities: decoding params changed, or we introduced a response-shaping layer during rollout that enforces brevity. any rollout PR links?
maria_supp: PR linked here: https://github.com/redwood/rollouts/pull/432 — mentions some cost-control heuristics, but no details in ticket.
acme_prod: model was redwood-open-7b-qa v4. sampling: top_p=0.95, temp=0.2, max_tokens=256. They say earlier outputs were more explanatory and polite.
sam_eng: checking deployment notes... we did flip a flag in the routing policy: response_shaping.compact_mode=true on support routes to trim average tokens. that would explain it.
maria_supp: customer is upset, wants rollback or opt-out for their org. can we do a temporary revert?
julie_ml: i'll run a quick experiment: batch the customer's prompt set on v4 with compact_mode off vs on and compare token distributions.
acme_prod: sending two more examples in case it helps.
acme_prod: Example 2:
Prompt: "Explain cost allocation for Q1"
Before: "For Q1, allocate shared infra costs by team usage metrics. Start with tagging, map to owners, apportion shared services, and reconcile monthly. See attached spreadsheet." (~120 tokens)
After: "Split infra costs by tag. Reconcile monthly." (~30 tokens)

maria_supp: noted. @julie_ml please run eval. sam_eng can we prepare a rollback for acme_org only?
sam_eng: making an ops ticket to disable compact_mode for org=acme_prod. Ticket INC-2026-54. ETA ~45m to roll back safe gradual config change.
julie_ml: initial run done: mean token length across 100 acme prompts dropped from 78 -> 29 with compact_mode on. median dropped similarly. Cause: compact_mode applies a multiplicative penalty that biases greedy decoding to shorter completions when expected token budget high.
sam_eng: ok will proceed with per-org toggle rollback. Also filing a short-term mitigation: add per-route override to keep explanatory style for support routes.
maria_supp: i'll tell the customer we're rolling back for them in ~45m and will re-run their examples. drafting message: apology + cause (cost-control flag) + rollback ETA + offer to re-run.
acme_prod: please include why this happened and what we will do to prevent it.
maria_supp: will add that we're adding per-org exceptions and audit checks for linguistic regressions.
SystemBot: rollback started by sam_eng at 1964023550
sam_eng: rollback completed at 1964023570 — can someone from acme confirm behavior?
acme_prod: quick smoke test: looks like responses are back to longer, explanatory form. confirmed. thanks for the fast turnaround.
maria_supp: closing the immediate escalation. will follow up with a short post-mortem and the per-org toggle feature request.
julie_ml: capturing eval results and a repro notebook in the incident doc. recommending we add an automated check for mean token length delta > 20% on model rollouts.
sam_eng: agreed. creating follow-up ticket FR-2026-88 for per-org response_shaping flag and a rollout canary metric.
maria_supp: thanks everyone. I'll update the customer thread and mark this resolved for now. :thumbsup:
